result.generation_response: This document is a letter dated January 1, 2014, from Mayor Tim B. Flynn of Oxnard, California, addressed to the City Council. The mayor reflects on the progress made in 2013, including ethics reform, addressing fiscal abuses identified in the Ventura County District Attorney's Investigation Report, road repairs, and job creation. He outlines three key priorities for 2014: (1) Hiring a permanent city manager by March 1, 2014, with decisions needed on the council's and public's roles in the process; (2) Beginning the hiring process for a new city attorney no later than January 14, 2014, while also setting performance-based goals to minimize lawsuits; and (3) Implementing priority-based budgeting aligned with the strategic priorities established in April 2013, to ensure spending reflects community needs and increases citizen engagement.

The document outlines the Performance and Priority Based Budgeting Benchmarks and Timelines for the City of Oxnard, presented by Mayor Tim Flynn. From January through June 2014, the city planned a structured budgeting process: January focused on distilling strategic objectives into public policy initiatives; February and March involved study sessions on policy adoption and priority-based budgeting; April gathered input from civic organizations; May finalized spending priorities; and June aimed to present the final FY 2014-2015 budget for council approval by June 17, 2014. Additional 2014 priorities included street resurfacing via a $30M bonding plan, attracting higher-paying jobs, restoring the general fund reserve from 10% back to 18%, establishing a K-12 magnet program, addressing pension liabilities, reviving city marketing, securing funding for Santa Clara River levees, managing former redevelopment properties, and making the Golf Course and Performing Arts Center self-sustaining.
